sources.entry: Algernon - Small self-contained pure-Go web server with Lua, Markdown, HTTP/2, QUIC, Redis and PostgreSQL support. (Source Code) BSD-3-Clause Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: Algernon is a small, self-contained pure-Go web server that serves Markdown, templates, JSX/TypeScript and Lua-scripted pages, with built-in HTTP/2, HTTP/3 (QUIC) and database support.
summary.what_it_does: Algernon serves static files and dynamically rendered pages from a directory, choosing the renderer by filename (index.md, index.lua, index.pongo2, index.amber, index.jsx, index.tsx, index.prompt and others). It converts Sass/SCSS, GCSS, JSX and TypeScript on the fly without a separate build step. Lua scripts (and optionally Teal) act as request handlers, with functions for headers, forms, redirects, HTTP client calls, JSON files, file uploads and a file cache. Data can be stored in Redis/Valkey (recommended), a built-in Bolt database, or accessed through SQLite, PostgreSQL, MSSQL and MariaDB/MySQL. The README also describes users and permissions, rate limiting via tollbooth, an auto-refresh feature that reloads the browser on source changes, a REPL, plugins that talk JSON-RPC, and Ollama-based LLM helpers.
use_cases: serve a local Markdown or static site without a separate build step
prototype web pages with Lua handlers and live reload
run a small self-hosted web app with a built-in database
preview README.md files in a browser
serve HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 (QUIC) with a single binary
generate pages using local Ollama LLMs
how_to_run: git clone the repository, cd algernon, go build -mod=vendor
mkdir mypage && cd mypage && create index.lua containing print("Hello, Algernon")
stack: Redis/Valkey, BoltDB, SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, MSSQL
notable: Single self-contained executable with no external runtime dependencies, under 17MB Docker image according to the README
Filename-based rendering: index.md, index.lua, index.amber and similar files are handled automatically
Built-in HTTP/2 over TLS and HTTP/3 (QUIC), with plain HTTP as fallback
Falls back to the built-in Bolt database when no Redis server is available
Zipped .alg applications can be loaded at startup
caveats: Auto-refresh only works on Linux and macOS, according to the README
The Lua implementation (gopherlua) does not support package.loadlib
Requires Go 1.26 or later to build from source
keywords: alternative to nginx for static sites
